reason: H0 only sends one byte buffer to plist_from_xml and cannot exercise the argv-based command-line protocol implemented by parse_arguments. S1 contains fuzz-worthy option sequencing and validation behavior, including value-taking options, missing-value rejection, aliases, format-prefix interpretation, flags, help handling, and rejection of unknown arguments.
evidence: H0 calls only plist_from_xml(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data), size, &root_node) and plist_free(root_node).
parse_arguments consumes argc and argv rather than an XML buffer.
parse_arguments handles --infile/-i, --outfile/-o, and --format/-f, each with an (i + 1) == argc missing-value path.
The --format/-f value is interpreted with strncmp(argv[i+1], "bin", 3) and strncmp(argv[i+1], "xml", 3), creating prefix-sensitive input semantics.
parse_arguments also handles --debug/-d and --help/-h, and its final else rejects any unrecognized argv[i].
recommended_action: Add a dedicated argv-oriented fuzz target for parse_arguments or the plistutil command entry point. Decode fuzz input into bounded argc/argv vectors and cover option aliases, ordering, repetitions, missing values, unknown options, and format values including short strings and bin/xml prefixes.
